positions.name: Oracle Corporation
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Tue 9/15 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BLOWOUT + GUIDANCE RAISE. Fiscal Q1 FY2027, reported after the 9/10 close: revenue $19.35B vs $19.14B consensus and $14.93B a year ago (+30% y/y); adjusted EPS $1.92 vs $1.74 expected. Total cloud revenue +62% to $11.6B, of which cloud INFRASTRUCTURE (OCI) rose 121% to $7.4B. Remaining performance obligations surged $209B year over year to $664B. Management guided fiscal Q2 cloud revenue growth of 64-70% in constant currency and RAISED full-year FY27 adjusted EPS guidance. The setup is unusual: ORCL fell 5.38% on 9/10 INTO the print on ~2x average volume (56.8M shares vs a 25.1M 30-day average), so the pre-market entry of 161.69 is +5.7% versus the 9/10 close of 152.94 but roughly flat against where the stock traded two sessions ago. The stock is still 51% below its 52-week high of 331.00 set exactly one year ago - the AI-capex de-rating has already happened in this name, which is what makes a beat of this size tradable rather than a sell-the-news event.
positions.risks: The $664B RPO is a backlog, not revenue, and is concentrated in a handful of very large AI customers whose own funding is not guaranteed - a single contract cancellation headline would hit hard. Capital intensity is the bear case: OCI growth of this magnitude requires enormous capex and Oracle is funding it with debt into a 4.94% 10-year yield. August CPI prints at 8:30am ET, roughly one hour after this entry, with markets pricing a 67.1% probability of a Fed HIKE in September - a hot core print would compress the whole long-duration software complex regardless of Oracle's quarter. Gap-fill risk to 152.94 is a real 5.4% drawdown.
positions.driver: Fiscal Q1 FY27 beat on both lines with OCI +121%, RPO $664B, Q2 cloud guide 64-70% cc and a raised FY27 EPS outlook, entered into a stock still 51% off its 52-week high.

positions.name: RH
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 MASSIVE EARNINGS BEAT + PRE-MARKET GAP. RH reported fiscal Q2 after the 9/10 close with EPS of $2.70 versus the $1.78 Street estimate - a 51.7% beat, the largest in today's tape. Revenue of $922.15M rose from $899.15M a year earlier but came in slightly under the $936.25M consensus, and the company narrowed fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $3.63-3.68B against a $3.63B analyst estimate, so the guide was nudged up at the low end. The stock is bid +8.0% pre-market to 144.77 from the 9/10 close of 134.02. What makes this tradable is the float: RH has only 15.5M shares in the float against 18.9M outstanding, and 9/10 volume was 2.11M shares versus a 690K 30-day average - 3.1x relative volume - so a gap of this size in a name this thin tends to extend before it mean-reverts. The stock closed 9/10 DOWN 3.84% into the print and sits 42% below its 52-week high of 248.44.
positions.risks: The single biggest caveat and the reason this is an INTRADAY position rather than a swing: the quarter included a $55.1M one-time tariff benefit, which is a material share of the beat and is not repeatable - once analysts strip it out the headline EPS number shrinks considerably. Revenue missed consensus. RH trades at a 46.3x price-to-book on a 26.9x P/E with a highly levered balance sheet and negative tangible equity history. The 15.5M float that amplifies the gap up will amplify a reversal just as violently, and an 8% pre-market gap in a thin name is exactly the profile that fades by the afternoon. High-end furniture demand is directly exposed to the 4.94% 10-year yield and to 67.1% odds of a Fed hike. I am not holding this over a weekend.
positions.driver: 51.7% EPS beat ($2.70 vs $1.78) gapping a 15.5M-share float up 8.0% pre-market on 3.1x prior-session volume, taken intraday only because the beat leans on a one-time $55.1M tariff benefit.

positions.name: Copart, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on the ACV tender-offer launch or HSR-clearance headline, by Wed 9/16 at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 M&A ANNOUNCEMENT. Copart announced after the 9/10 close a definitive agreement to acquire ACV Auctions (ACVA) for $10.50 per share in cash, valuing ACV at approximately $1.9B in equity - a 45% premium to ACV's unaffected 8/10 close and 41% over its 30-day VWAP. The deal is all cash from Copart's balance sheet with NO financing condition; Copart ended July with roughly $5.7B of liquidity ($4.5B cash and held-to-maturity securities plus a $1.25B undrawn revolver) and zero debt outstanding, and management said on the call it retains over $2B of cash post-deal. Both boards approved unanimously; it is structured as a tender offer, which is the fastest path to closing, targeted for year-end 2026. Copart is bid +4.7% pre-market to 32.20 from the 9/10 close of 30.75 DESPITE a fiscal Q4 EPS miss (35c versus 38c consensus, revenue $1.15B beating $1.14B) - the market is explicitly repricing the acquirer higher on strategic merit, which is the opposite of the usual acquirer reaction and the clearest signal in this setup. The stock closed 9/10 down 4.0% and sits 34% below its 49.05 52-week high.
positions.risks: The underlying operating quarter was genuinely weak and that bill comes due: global units sold fell 2.9%, US units fell 5.7%, US insurance volume fell 7.5%, operating expense per car rose 12.7% year over year, Q4 operating income fell 10.6% and net income fell 17.4%. Management explicitly declined to guide on cost recovery beyond saying 'we're on it'. The CFO clarified on the call that ACV is only BREAKEVEN in the first full year and accretive in FY28 - further out than the initial framing implied. Acquirer pops on deal news frequently round-trip within 48 hours once the operating miss is digested, which is why this is catalyst-defined with a tight leash rather than a week-long hold. HSR antitrust review of two vehicle-auction platforms combining is a non-trivial regulatory risk.
positions.driver: $1.9B all-cash acquisition of ACV Auctions at $10.50/share with no financing condition, lifting the ACQUIRER 4.7% pre-market even through a fiscal Q4 EPS miss.

positions.name: GameStop Corp.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS REVENUE BEAT + BALANCE-SHEET CATALYST. GameStop reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $790.2M against a $756.85M consensus, with adjusted EPS of 27 cents matching estimates. The tradable element is the balance sheet rather than the P&L: the company disclosed it holds approximately 43.4 million eBay shares worth roughly $4.9B and completed exchanges retiring about $1.4B in convertible notes, cutting total long-term debt to roughly $2.8B. Against a $9.15B market cap, a $4.9B marketable equity stake plus a $1.4B debt retirement is a genuine repricing event, and the stock trades at a 1.45x price-to-book and a 13.2x P/E. GME is bid +3.8% pre-market to 21.17 from the 9/10 close of 20.39, the strongest move among the post-earnings retail names. It traded 11.6M shares on 9/10 versus a 6.96M 30-day average - 1.66x relative volume - and closed UP 2.51% into the print, so the bid is continuation rather than reversal. The stock sits just 19% above its 17.79 52-week low from 8/20.
positions.risks: The operating business is still shrinking hard: revenue of $790.2M is down 18.7% from $972.2M a year earlier, and adjusted EPS merely matched rather than beat. The entire thesis rests on a marked-to-market eBay stake, which means GME now carries embedded equity-market beta on top of its own - a broad risk-off move on a hot CPI print at 8:30am ET hits the stock twice. This is a heavily retail-owned, high-social-velocity name where intraday reversals of 5%+ on no news are routine, which is why it is sized smaller than the other Tier 1 entries at $2,500 and held intraday only.
positions.driver: Q2 revenue beat plus disclosure of a $4.9B eBay stake and $1.4B of converts retired against a $9.15B market cap, +3.8% pre-market on 1.66x prior-session volume.
